scope: Severe community-acquired pneumonia and influenza-associated respiratory failure, as summarised in a 2026 open evidence framework.

keyRecommendations.text: In the CAPE COD trial of ICU patients with severe CAP, continuous intravenous hydrocortisone 200 mg/day was associated with lower 28-day mortality than placebo (6.2% vs 11.9%).
keyRecommendations.population: ICU patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia

keyRecommendations.text: Subgroup analyses in that trial are exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously.
For influenza-associated ARDS, the review states that multiple societies advise against routine systemic corticosteroids unless there is a separate indication.

clinicalBottomLine: The accepted review supports early hydrocortisone in severe CAP on the basis of CAPE COD, and advises against routine corticosteroids for influenza-associated ARDS unless another indication is present.
notableCaveats: Figures are those reported by the review for CAPE COD, not a re-analysis. Non-severe CAP dosing is not the focus of the quoted CAPE COD section.
